message.what: G3-G5 geomagnetic storm conditions have ended. G1-G2 activity and elevated solar particle levels may continue as the event subsides.
message.where: Worldwide and Earth's orbit. Higher-latitude regions above 55 degrees remain the primary area of concern for residual effects.
message.when: Warning-level conditions ended by 0000 UTC Tue May 14 2024. Lower-level activity may continue through 1200 UTC Tue May 14 2024.
message.current_status: Solar wind conditions remain disturbed, but the geomagnetic response has weakened substantially from peak levels. Current guidance does not support renewed G3 or greater conditions through 1200 UTC Tue May 14 2024.
message.impacts: Residual effects may continue, especially at higher latitudes and for sensitive operations. Power systems may experience weak fluctuations. HF communication and GNSS performance may remain degraded at higher latitudes. Low-Earth-orbit satellites may continue to experience increased drag. Elevated particle levels may remain a concern for aviation, satellite, and other radiation-sensitive operations.
message.additional_details: The Space Weather Warning is no longer in effect. Partners may return to normal monitoring as sector-specific and local procedures allow. SWPC will continue monitoring the Sun and near-Earth space environment while residual activity subsides.
message.next_update: A final Space Weather Summary will be issued no later than 1600 UTC Thu May 16 2024. An additional Statement will be issued sooner if conditions materially change.
